title: Unable to access certain sites on Chrome using Exit Nodes
body: I am using a Tailscale exit node from my macOS Ventura 13.5.2 device with Tailscale 1.48.2 (macsys). Certain websites fail in Chrome with ERR_CONNECTION_RESET while the exit node is active, but the same websites work in Safari. Other people at my company do not seem to have the problem, so I suspect it affects only certain devices. This is my first time using exit nodes, and I am not certain how to reproduce it beyond using Chrome through the exit node. Avast AV is installed. Bug report: BUG-6d2218208b897581dbf3fbb18f1df079c6904f36c5046d770be2e42a4199d3a4-20230919210540Z-903996c7ac93c724.

symptoms_visible: Certain websites show ERR_CONNECTION_RESET in Chrome while I use the Tailscale exit node, but the same websites open in Safari.
Other people at my company do not seem to encounter the problem on their devices.
N0.label: N0 Chrome failures through exit node reported

symptoms_visible: Gmail, YouTube, Google Drive, and other Google sites fail continuously in Chrome through the exit node.
AWS sometimes works and sometimes fails.
N1.label: N1 affected sites identified

symptoms_visible: The Chrome error still occurs after I broke IPv6 on the exit node.
I reproduced the error while capturing traffic on the Mac's Tailscale interface.
N2.label: N2 failure captured after IPv6 disruption

symptoms_visible: ERR_CONNECTION_RESET still occurs in Chrome through the exit node even though Chrome has no configured proxy and Avast has already been disabled for a long time.
I captured the failure again and sent the second packet capture for analysis.
N3.label: N3 local proxy and Avast excluded

symptoms_visible: After I disabled Experimental QUIC in Chrome, everything worked for about ten minutes.
The issue returned after I relaunched Chrome even though the QUIC flag was still disabled.
N4.label: N4 QUIC probe only briefly changes behavior

symptoms_visible: External IPv6 connectivity was established through the exit node and the Chrome issue was reported resolved, but I did not post my own public retest afterward.
N_terminal.label: terminal maintainer-reported resolution without public reporter retest

question_patterns: Which websites consistently fail, and which ones still work?
Can you give examples of affected sites?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is mostly Google sites such as Gmail, YouTube, and Google Drive. Google sites fail continuously. AWS partly works but fails at other times, and I do not have an exact list of every affected site.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every website fails in both Chrome and Safari whenever the exit node is active.
The same Google sites fail continuously, but AWS has worked every time I tested it.

edges.comment: Reporter c4 identifies continuously failing Google properties and intermittent AWS behavior. This is the opening reporter's own device and symptom chain.

question_patterns: Can you capture traffic on the Mac's Tailscale interface while reproducing the failure and send the packet capture privately?
Please start Wireshark on the utun interface, visit an affected site, stop the capture, and send the pcap.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I activated the exit node, captured packets with Wireshark while visiting a Google site, and sent the packet capture by email. The error was still occurring during the capture.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I cannot reproduce the error while Wireshark is recording; all affected sites work during every capture.
I reproduced the same error and captured it on a differently numbered utun interface.

question_patterns: Was this packet capture taken on the affected Mac or on the exit node?
Can you confirm which machine produced the pcap?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The pcap was gathered from the Mac where I am using Google Chrome.

edges.comment: Reporter c11 and c14 captures the failure on the affected Mac and confirms the capture location. In c11 the reporter also volunteers that deliberately breaking IPv6 on the exit node did not change the error; this persistent exit-node change is why the target uses system state S1b.

question_patterns: Can you check Chrome's network settings and confirm whether any proxy is configured?
Are there any browser or system proxy settings enabled on this Mac?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can confirm that there are no proxy settings enabled.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Chrome is configured to use a corporate HTTP proxy, and bypassing that proxy makes the sites work.

question_patterns: Was the capture recorded while ERR_CONNECTION_RESET was visible, and can you send the newer capture for analysis?
Please reproduce the error again, capture it, and send the second pcap through the support email.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, the packets were captured while I encountered ERR_CONNECTION_RESET using the exit node. I captured a second pcap and sent it to the support address with a reference to this issue.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The second capture was taken after the page had recovered, so it does not include the failure.

question_patterns: Can you disable Avast temporarily and report whether Chrome's behavior changes?
Is Avast currently active on the affected Mac?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Avast has already been disabled on my machine for a long time.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Avast was active, and disabling it immediately and consistently stops the Chrome errors.
Avast is disabled, and I changed its notification settings as well.

edges.comment: Reporter c21-c25 confirms no configured local proxy, confirms the capture coincided with the error, supplies the second pcap, and establishes that Avast was already disabled. Packet interpretation remains engineer-side.

question_patterns: As a diagnostic test, can you disable Experimental QUIC in Chrome, relaunch it, and report whether the issue persists?
Please change Chrome's Experimental QUIC flag to Disabled and tell me what happens before and after restarting Chrome.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I disabled the flag and everything worked for about ten minutes. After I relaunched Chrome, the issue came back even though I checked and the flag was still disabled.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Disabling QUIC fixes the problem consistently across repeated Chrome restarts.
It worked for fifteen minutes instead of ten, but the issue returned after relaunch while the flag remained disabled.

edges.comment: Reporter c27 gives the raw result of the handler-initiated Chrome flag probe. It is a measurement clarification, not a fix: the improvement was temporary and the failure returned with the flag still disabled.

solution.intent: Restore genuine external IPv6 connectivity through the exit node so Chrome's preferred IPv6 connections reach their destinations, then have the affected user retest before declaring the case resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Fix the exit node's upstream IPv6 routing rather than disabling QUIC or blaming Avast. Chrome was treating IPv6 as usable because an intermediary completed the initial stream handshake before the true IPv6 destination had been reached; the stream then closed and Chrome did not fall back to IPv4. After establishing working external IPv6 connectivity through the exit node, retest Gmail, YouTube, and Google Drive in Chrome on the affected Mac.
solution.inference_hint: Engineers inferred from the private pcaps that the exit node returned ICMPv6 Destination Unreachable, that valid A and AAAA DNS answers arrived together, and that an intermediary proxy completed enough of the connection handshake for Chrome to regard IPv6 as healthy. The reporter supplied captures and probe results but did not derive this mechanism. The public tail states that establishing IPv6 connectivity resolved the issue, but the reporter did not post a public confirmation after that change.

edges.comment: Final accepted diagnosis from participant4 c26 and c28 on the opening reporter's deployment: the exit node lacked external IPv6 connectivity, while a non-Tailscale intermediary proxy made the IPv6 stream initially appear established, preventing Chrome's expected IPv4 fallback. Establishing IPv6 connectivity was reported to resolve it. Because no affected-user retest appears publicly after that change, the terminal remains user_perceives_resolved=false.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: the exit node lacked working external IPv6 connectivity, while an intermediary proxy handshake made Chrome regard IPv6 as functional, so failed IPv6 streams did not trigger the expected IPv4 fallback.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the packet captures and behavioral probes: the failure was captured on the affected Mac, engineers observed IPv6 destination-unreachable behavior with valid IPv4 and IPv6 DNS answers, and disabling QUIC only helped briefly.

Must recommend establishing genuine external IPv6 connectivity through the exit node rather than treating Avast, a configured Chrome proxy, deliberate IPv6 breakage, or permanent QUIC disabling as the fix.
Must ask the affected user to retest Chrome through the corrected exit node before declaring user-verified resolution.
Must not claim that the reporter publicly confirmed the final fix; the thread only contains the maintainer's statement that establishing IPv6 connectivity resolved the issue.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical macOS user who can collect Tailscale bug reports, change Chrome flags, alter exit-node networking, and capture traffic with Wireshark when given precise instructions.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite and cooperative, usually concise; reports concrete observations, follows diagnostic steps, and openly states uncertainty when behavior is inconsistent.
